Messages.Author: Hardy Range
Messages.Body:
Aye
Master: trifle.
Put this card on a Laibon. This Laibon may tap this card to cancel a
Frenzy card played on him or her as it is played. This Laibon may burn
a blood and tap three of his or her Aye to be able to play rection
cards and attempt to blcok as if untapped for the current action. If
this Laibon burns a minion, equipment, or location in play, he or she
burns one Aye. Burn this card if this Laibon has more Orun and Aye than
his or her capacity.
Illus: Brad Williams

Messages.Author: John Flournoy
Messages.Body:


Man, I hope not - don't get me wrong, I like the KotE setting; but the
KotE vampires have about as much in common with Western Kindred as do
Mummies or Wraiths, and I don't particularly think any of those should
be represented in game as more than allies and/or retainers.

When you say 'KotE are more exotic than regular kindred', if by 'more
exotic' you mean 'almost entirely, completely different', then yes. I
mean, they're both sort-of-dead, and they both feed on energy from the
living in one way or another.. but beyond that, there's almost nothing
in common aside from the most basic WW RPG rules framework. (Kuei-Jin
don't even care about tracking/using blood points, which is one of the
absolute basic, core elements of the Vampire/VTES setting, as is
another thing Kuei-Jin lack: "Generation/Capacity".)

I mean, yes, you could invent a whole conversion system where 'the
counters on a Kuei-Jin represent Chi points, and if you put them on the
top half they're Yin and the bottom is Yang' and so on, but that's a
really kludgy forced-compatability effort - if you're going to cram
Kuei-Jin rules to fit VTES, why not cram Call of Cthulhu RPG rules into
the CCG? "I hit you with Undead Strength for 3" "Well, I can't prevent
that, so I burn 3 Sanity points from my Investigator.." Why not Street
Fighter rules, or Buffy RPG rules, or Shadowrun? "My vampire Thefts
your Elf for 2!"

-John Flournoy

I don't see how they are inherently 'more compatible', given that KotE
have almost nothing in common with the western Kindred.

Kuei-jin lack clan, capacity/generation, blood, don't care about
western politics/sects, can't learn existing VTES disciplines nor can
their powers ever be on a western Kindred..

How is that any different than (for instance) Shadowrun or Cthulhu? If
you're having to make up conversion rules to allow a Kuei-Jin's card to
have an equivalent of all the attributes on a crypt card, how is that
any easier or harder than making up conversion rules for any other
system?

Here, let me give a concrete example: D&D characters.

Clan == Alignment.
Capacity == HP/10.
Sect: Independent. Heck, maybe we make up a sect called 'Greyhawk.'
Disciplines: Classes/feats/etc, low level/high level.

So my LG FTR 10/WIZ 2 with 66 HP? He can be represented as follows:

Grarg the Slayer of Kings
Clan: Lawful Good Adventurers
Capacity: 6
Disciplines: FTR wiz rog (we'll give him rog cause he has a couple of
cross-class skills.)
Greyhawk. +1 Strength. (he's a half-orc with a 20 Str.)

That's not so hard, is it? We can represent the FTR discipline by
making a bunch of combat cards to represent fighter feats - Cleave can
provide an additional strike, Power Attack can function like a better
Haymaker.. we can have his Plate Mail be equipment that prevents 2
points of damage per combat except from guns; the Wizard discipline can
be a mixed bag of card types representing spells - heck, we can create
Retainer cards for the familiars, etc etc etc.

That took me 3 minutes. What makes KotE 'more compatible' than this,
necessarily?

-John Flournoy

Messages.Author: John Flournoy
Messages.Body:
tobiasopdenbr...@notsocoldmail.com wrote:

> I understand your objections. KotE are more compatible with the WoD
> universe than Cthulhu or (shadowrun) elves, though. A matter of taste,
> in the end.
>
> I don't see any reason to not simplify the KotE until they fit into
> V:TES as well as the Laibon do, though. Since the old WoD is dead, and
> V:TES carries on the torch, no problem treating them differently in
> V:TES.

I'll be a little more serious.

At the moment, VTES vampires have the following:

Name - no problem here regardless of setting.
Clan - any setting where the characters are easily grouped by similar
traits works here.
Blood capacity - okay, this is harder, and the place where stuff gets
kludged a lot.
Disciplines - any setting with distinct power/ability groupings for
characters, where each group has an ascending scale is an easy
translation.
Group - no brainer. whatever you want.
Advancement - again, no-brainer, you can skip that.
Sect - either cram it into an existing sect, or make a new one up.
Ability - hundreds of choices here, it's an easy fit.

So the real sticking points in terms of 'simplifying until they fit
into VTES' are Clan, Blood Capacity and Disciplines.

Kuei-Jin (for instance) have no Clan or Capacity, and Disciplines that
are totally incompatible with existing VTES ones - not a big deal, as
you can create new disciplines and discipline-required cards that
translate the specific levels of these powers. Small problem with 'why
can't my Tremere use an infernal familiar or Infernal Pact to do
Kuei-jin stuff', but that's errata-able. So if you fake a system for
Clan/Capacity, it's not that hard of a conversion.

D&D Wizards (for instance) have no Clan or Capacity, and Schools of
Magic that are totally incompatible with existing VTES disciplines -
not a big deal, as you can create a new discipline for each school
(Abjuration, Enchantment, etc) and discipline-required cards that
translate the specific levels of these powers ("spells"). Small problem
with 'why can't my Tremere use an infernal familiar or Infernal Pact to
do D&D WIzard stuff', but that's errata-able. So if you fake a system
for Clan/Capacity, it's not that hard of a conversion.

Shadowrunners (for instance) have no Clan or Capacity, and magic spells
and cyberware that are totally incompatible with existing VTES powers -
not a big deal, as you can create new disciplines (shaman magic,
cyberware, decker programs) and discipline-required cards that
translate the specific uses of these abilities. Small problem with 'why
can't my Tremere use an infernal familiar or Infernal Pact to use
Cyberware/Shamanistic Magic', but that's errata-able. So if you fake a
system for Clan/Capacity, it's not that hard of a conversion.

Battletech Mechs (for instance) have Clans/Houses but no Capacity, and
components that are totally incompatible with existing VTES powers -
not a big deal, as you can create new disciplines (armor, weapons, heat
sinks, sensors, mobility, etc) and discipline-required cards that
translate the specific components into VTES powers. Small problem with
'why can't my Tremere use an infernal familiar or Infernal Pact to use
BattleMech components', but that's errata-able. So if you fake a system
for Capacity (tonnage!) - Clan is trivial, it's not that hard of a
conversion. Heck, there's even two easy-to-convert sects, "Inner
Sphere" and "Clan Warriors"!

So basically, if you're going to 'simplify' KotE into VTES, the _only_
reason why this system would be better than a wide range of completely
unrelated settings is a thematic one - the rules and mechanics are
actually _harder_ to simplify for KotE than they would be for some
other settings.

And a big, non-exaggerated part of my point is this: if you are going
to add in new settings, the deciding factor is really going to be
'thematic'; and while KotE has the thematic advantage of being part of
the World of Darkness, other games also share that advantage (Wraith,
Werewolf, Mage, Mummies, Gypsies, Demon: the Fallen, Changeling, etc
etc) while being just as easy to simplify into VTES.

And aside from the word "Kindred", Kuei-jin have about as much in
common with western vampires as do Mummies or Wraiths - they're all in
the World of Darkness, they're all dead-and-yet-still-active, they all
have some sort of power reserve(s) that need constant replenishing,
etc. Beyond that, the thematic material for Kuei-jin really _isn't_
that similar to Vampire - they have radically different motivations,
social groupings, histories, origins, sources of their powers and uses
for them, etc.

So thematically, there's not a lot of reason why Wraiths would be a
worse new crypt choice than Kuei-jin - aside from 'personal taste'.

And my own personal taste is this: Why is the game _better_ if we
include other largely-incompatible, thematically different game
settings that have to be simplified and/or converted to fit the
existing rules, and will require a _lot_ of 'because we say so for
'game balance'' statements about why the very, very different thematic
elements that shouldn't mesh do work in the CCG (for instance, why
should a Kuei-Jin care about the effects of the First Tradition? Uh,
cause we say so for game balance.)? How is this a beneficial addition
to the game, especially when there are plenty of still-untapped parts
of the existing Vampire setting that haven't been included yet that
require zero conversion? Why dilute the game outside the existing
setting (Old WoD Cainite Vampire) in the first place?

-John Flournoy

See my other post.

Chi is sort of similar to blood, except that you don't have capacity,
and Chi _isn't_ blood; it doesn't have to come from blood, and draining
the blood from a Kuei-jin doesn't affect their blood. P'o is similar to
'the beast', but 'the beast' isn't in and of itself game mechanic in
VTES, so that's irrelevant for converting crypt cards. Gehenna works,
but the specifics of the Gehenna stuff for the Kuei-jin is not
identical to Vampire, just as the Garou Apocalypse is
similarly-end-of-the-world-but-different-because-they're-different-creatures
from Vampire - I don't recall the Kuei-jin Gehenna scenarios caring one
whit if Caine shows up, for instance.

And again, in all seriousness - Kuei-jin are equally compatible (or
incompatible) with Vampire as Mummies, Gypsies, Wraiths, Changelings,
Garou, etc etc. Why include _any_ of these, when any of them would
require 'simplification', errata, and scores of 'well, this overlaps
because we say so despite it making no sense logically' rulings? Why
would this be a positive addition to the game instead of a dilution of
the thematic focus (since the themes of these other WoD settings,
including KotE, are so distinct and different from Vampire?) And why
Kuei-Jin over one of the others, since Kuei-jin have almost no relevant
traits in common with Vampire - not in parallel, in common - every WoD
setting has tons of stuff in parallel, but Kuei-jin share basically
nothing with Vampire that isn't also shared by every other WoD setting?

-John Flournoy

> should a Kuei-Jin care about the effects of the First Tradition? Uh,
> cause we say so for game balance.)? How is this a beneficial addition
> to the game, especially when there are plenty of still-untapped parts
> of the existing Vampire setting that haven't been included yet that
> require zero conversion? Why dilute the game outside the existing
> setting (Old WoD Cainite Vampire) in the first place?

As to the 'why is it better if we include this new stuff' part -
because fresh is fun, witness the bloodlines, the laibon, new allies
over expansions, etc.

As to the simplified/converted/game balance - laibon, scarce, etc.,
were concepts introduced without a problem (I think - bit early for
Laibon, of course). The 'because we say so for game balance' argument
isn't a bad one (witness vampire design) to start with, and also may
not be needed in case of the example you pose: 'The first tradition is
being actively enforced by camarilla and the methuselah's backing it.
So much so, that even the KotE are restricted.'

Arguing that KotE wouldn't be restricted because they are so
thematically different is the same as arguing that Laibon wouldn't be
hit (they're a whole continent away too!) or mortal allies, werewolves,
etc. And they are.

Messages.Author: Fabio 'Sooner' Macedo
Messages.Body:
A few tidbits about the KotE setting...

tobiasopdenbr...@notsocoldmail.com wrote:
> John Flournoy wrote:

> > And aside from the word "Kindred", Kuei-jin have about as much in
> > common with western vampires

Not even that - they don't use that word to define themselves, as far
as I can remember.

as do Mummies or Wraiths - they're all in
> > the World of Darkness, they're all dead-and-yet-still-active, they all
> > have some sort of power reserve(s) that need constant replenishing,
> > etc.
>
> And the Keui-Jin's reserve is replenished, for the majority of them, by
> drinking blood.

"The majority" being all Kuei-Jin who either didn't make it far in
their Dharma and do have a Dharma to progress by at all. So yes, the
average Kuei-Jin replenishes Chi by drinking blood. But the older,
advanced ones (say, translating to VTES, the higher caps) and the
recently changed (again, translating to VTES, the weenies) do not drink
blood at all. The "high-caps" take Chi from the air, and the "weenies"
need to consume flesh to get chi - and the latter are usually
beast-minded, uncontrolled beings.

Long story short, blood is only one source for Chi. It can be the most
commonly used, but it's far from the best one - if they could, all
Kuei-Jin would prefer to get chi from the air.

Not translating it to the CCG would be a desservice to KotE's
background. It can be done, though, via vampire's specials or a new
mechanic.

> > Beyond that, the thematic material for Kuei-jin really _isn't_
> > that similar to Vampire - they have radically different motivations,
> > social groupings, histories, origins, sources of their powers and uses
> > for them, etc.
>
> The first 4 reasons are also true for the Laibon.

It depends on the point of view.

Different motivations? Yes. But they also share many concerns
(Masquerade Tradition/Secret Must be Kept, Domain/No Secrets from the
Magaji, etc.)

Social groupings? Not as different as the dharmas or the way Kuei-Jin
organize themselves. The Legacies are local versions of the main
western clans. The titles/positions of honour (magaji, kholo) are local
versions of western positions (magaji is way closer to prince or baron
than any position hold by the Kuei-Jin could ever be).

Histories? Of course they're different, it's a different culture. But
*still*, all Legacies ultimately come from Caine. The Kuei-Jin Dharmas
do not. The Kuei-Jin as a race come from both the material and the
spirit world alike; they're akin to Risen wraiths in that respect.

Sources of their
> powers - true (but demonic powers could be grasped by a discipline -
> see daimonion).
Uses of their powers - there's a lot of functional
> overlap with kindred powers, even if the names are different.

You can translate each Kuei-Jin power into any western discipline you
want. That's the whole point of the debate - it *can* be done. But that
wouldn't do justice to the setting.

> Didn't you get the 'same vampires, different coat of paint' feel with
> KotE? I did. Even White-Wolf thought so (even if only from a marketing
> point) when they named the book KINDRED of the East.

Despite the book's name, I recall that they do not refer to themselves
using that term.
"Kindred" is just a way to market it to the player base. If they called
the book "The Kuei-Jin [of the East]", no player would have a clue of
what the book is about.

> Other than wraiths having precedent as an ally type, and the fact
> they're mostly incorporeal and have a very different type of
> interaction with mortals than kindred?

Kuei-Jin have different corporeal functions (depending on the balance
of yin/yang chi, they can even breed with humans and eat food - and it
can happen for any Kuei-Jin no matter if they're "young" or not, so
it's not the same thing as being thin-blooded) and interact with
mortals in a different way, too. Shouldn't they be allies too? That's
the whole point in this debate...

Myself, I'd love to see Kuei-Jin as crypt cards. But the practical part
sounds that it would require either too much twinking, or
oversimplification. For the former, I don't want more complexity than
necessary. For the latter, we can always do allies. There's already
oversimplificated ally versions of hunters, werewolves, mortals anyway.

> As to the 'why is it better if we include this new stuff' part -

I think it's a little more complicated than that.
There are tons of "new stuff" to include using the western vampires'
background of the game still.
Of course, that does not mean that KotE should *ever* be included.

> because fresh is fun, witness the bloodlines, the laibon, new allies
> over expansions, etc.

... all of which didn't require more than just a few twists.
The Laibon required (up to this point in the preview) a new sect that
works much the same way any other does; a new icon/rule (reflex) to
simulate the effects of one (just *one*, not several) new discipline;
and that's all.

How could we adapt the Kuei-Jin just by creating a new sect and *one*
discipline with a new mechanic into it?

> As to the simplified/converted/game balance - laibon, scarce, etc.,
> were concepts introduced without a problem (I think - bit early for
> Laibon, of course). The 'because we say so for game balance' argument
> isn't a bad one (witness vampire design) to start with, and also may
> not be needed in case of the example you pose: 'The first tradition is
> being actively enforced by camarilla and the methuselah's backing it.
> So much so, that even the KotE are restricted.'

Yeah, the Tradition part is not a problem since we already have strange
representantions of sect interaction in the game as it is now - Priscus
voting during Praxis Seizures and all that.

> Arguing that KotE wouldn't be restricted because they are so
> thematically different is the same as arguing that Laibon wouldn't be
> hit (they're a whole continent away too!) or mortal allies, werewolves,
> etc. And they are.

I think the Laibon do not bring to the game any more
background-to-rules weirdness than the game already has, as pointed out
by the Priscus example above.

best,

Fabio "Sooner" Macedo

Messages.Author: Disco Stu
Messages.Body:
> Long story short, blood is only one source for Chi. It can be the most
> commonly used, but it's far from the best one - if they could, all
> Kuei-Jin would prefer to get chi from the air.

I tried to cover that in my virtual expansion. Blood is standard for
hunts, however elder KJ can get funky action modifiers on hunt actions.

Perhaps 1-cap KJ get -1 stealth when hunting to represent the
flesh-eating?

> How could we adapt the Kuei-Jin just by creating a new sect and *one*
> discipline with a new mechanic into it?

It'd be a disservice to the source material if we did. Do them well or
don't do them at all.

For those unfamiliar with the RPG, Laibon are, essentially, variations
on existing clans. They have generation, disciplines, etc. Different
culture, and one new mechanic (Orun/Aye), but otherwise essentially
physiologically identical.
KOTE are a different species entirely, although one that mirrors
'western' vampires in many ways. Think thylacine vs. canine - cosmetic
similarities but very different creatures.

Disco
